''Les Athéniens'' (The Athenians) | short name = VAFC | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1913}} | stadium = [[Stade du Hainaut]] | capacity = 25,172 | owner = [[Sport Republic]] | chairman = Henrik Kraft | chrtitle = President | manager = Samuel Goethals | mgrtitle = Head coach | league = {{French football updater|Valenciennes}} | season = {{French football updater|Valenciennes2}} | position = {{French football updater|Valenciennes3}} | website = {{URL|http://www.va-fc.com}} | current = 2026–27 Valenciennes FC season | pattern_la1 = _ValenciennesFC2526h | pattern_b1 = _ValenciennesFC2526h | pattern_ra1 = _ValenciennesFC2526h | pattern_sh1 = _ValenciennesFC2526h | pattern_so1 = _Valenciennes2526h | leftarm1 = | body1 = | rightarm1 = | shorts1 = | socks1 = | pattern_la2 = _ValenciennesFC2526a | pattern_b2 = _ValenciennesFC2526a | pattern_ra2 = _ValenciennesFC2526a | pattern_sh2 = _ValenciennesFC2526a | pattern_so2 = _Valenciennes2526a | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | socks2 = }} '''Valenciennes Football Club''' ({{IPA|fr|valɑ̃sjɛn|-|ValenciennesNPDC.ogg}}; commonly known as '''Valenciennes''', '''VA''' or '''VAFC'''; {{IPA|fr|ve.a.ɛf.se}}) is a [[Football in France|French]] professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Valenciennes]]. The club was founded in 1914 and currently play in [[Ligue 3]], the third tier of French football. Valenciennes plays its home matches at the recently built [[Stade du Hainaut]] located within the city.{{cite news |title=Nungesser II inauguré avec l'Ajax d'Amsterdam |url=http://www.leparisien.fr/sports/football/valenciennes-nungesser-ii-inaugure-avec-l-ajax-d-amsterdam-04-01-2011-1212915.php |work=Le Parisien |location=France |date=4 January 2011 |access-date=12 January 2011 |archive-date=22 September 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120922125416/http://www.leparisien.fr/sports/football/valenciennes-nungesser-ii-inaugure-avec-l-ajax-d-amsterdam-04-01-2011-1212915.php |url-status=dead }} Valenciennes was founded under the name '''Union Sportive de Valenciennes Anzin''' (USVA). The club spent over 80 years playing under the name before switching to its current name. Valenciennes has spent an almost equal amount of time playing in [[Ligue 1]] and [[Ligue 2]] having played 40 seasons in the first division and 36 seasons in the second division. The club has never won the first division, but has won Ligue 2 on two occasions. Valenciennes has also won the [[Championnat National]] and the [[Championnat de France amateur]] in 2005 and 1998, respectively. In [[1951 Coupe de France final|1951]], the club made its first and only appearance in a [[Coupe de France]] final. From 2004 to 2011, Valenciennes was presided over by Francis Decourrière, a former politician who served as a [[Member of the European Parliament]] under the [[Social Democratic Party (France)|Social Democratic Party]] from 1994 to 1999 and later the ''[[Union for French Democracy|Union pour la Démocratie Française]]'' (''Union for French Democracy'') from 1999 to 2004.{{cite news |title=Francis DECOURRIÈRE |url=http://www.europarl.europa.eu/members/archive/alphaOrder/view.do?language=EN&id=2026 |publisher=[[European Parliament]]|access-date=12 January 2011}} In 2011, Decourrière left the position and was replaced by Jean-Raymond Legrand."}}
